briefings.title: $1B DEFENSE PUSH: GE Aerospace makes major investment in US manufacturing
briefings.tldr: GE Aerospace is launching a $1 billion investment in 2026 across 30 U.S. communities to accelerate engine production and clear a $200 billion backlog, a move that includes $275 million for defense upgrades and the creation of 5,000 new American jobs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** GE Aerospace is launching a $1 billion investment in 2026 across 30 U.S. communities to accelerate engine production and clear a $200 billion backlog, a move that includes $275 million for defense upgrades and the creation of 5,000 new American jobs.

## Strategic Capital Investment & Job Creation
*   **Domestic Expansion:** GE Aerospace will invest $1 billion throughout 2026 across 17 states.
    *   The Durham, North Carolina facility—GE’s largest engine assembly site—is a primary focus for ramping up Leap engine production for Boeing and Airbus fleets.
*   **Workforce Growth:** The company aims to hire 5,000 new employees in 2026.
    *   This follows a previous hire of 5,000 workers in 2025, aimed at building technical expertise for production demands lasting into the 2030s.
*   **Modernization & AI:** Investment includes deploying AI on the shop floor to improve productivity, safety, and quality.
    *   **Data Utilization:** AI leverages data from 20- to 30-year engine lifecycles to enhance both new manufacturing and long-term maintenance.

## Defense Infrastructure & Military Readiness
*   **Defense Funding:** $275 million of the $1 billion investment is specifically earmarked for defense facility upgrades.
    *   This brings GE’s total three-year investment in its defense footprint to $600 million.
*   **Critical Military Support:** GE currently powers two-thirds of U.S. military aircraft, including combat jets and helicopters.
    *   **J85 Engine Contract:** A new deal with the Defense Logistics Agency will optimize the supply chain for the J85 engine, which powers the Air Force’s T-38 trainer aircraft.
*   **Procurement Reform:** CEO Larry Culp expressed strong support for streamlining government procurement to reduce lead times for tooling and testing without sacrificing safety.

## Operational Scaling & Supply Chain Recovery
*   **Massive Backlog:** The company is managing a nearly $200 billion backlog driven by surging commercial airline expansion and rising global defense budgets.
*   **Supply Chain Gains:** GE reported a 40% increase in inputs from key suppliers over the last year.
    *   This collaboration resulted in engine shipments increasing by 25% to 30% in 2025.
*   **Cost of Ownership:** Culp emphasized that for engines costing $10M+, the focus is on reliability over a 20- to 30-year lifecycle. GE currently powers approximately 75% of all global commercial departures.

## Financial Performance & Trade Policy
*   **Record Growth:** In 2025, GE Aerospace saw revenue grow by 21%, earnings by 38%, and cash flow by 24%.
*   **Trade Advocacy:** The company supports "zero-for-zero" tariff constructs to maintain the U.S. aerospace industry’s status as a top net exporter ($75 billion annually).
*   **Market Leverage:** Culp noted that President Trump views aerospace as a key point of leverage in international trade relations, particularly regarding China.

## Notable Quotes
> "We power the better part of three quarters of all commercial departures around the world on a daily basis. We have a million people in the air currently with GE technology under wing. It’s an incredible responsibility we all take very seriously." 
— **Larry Culp, CEO of GE Aerospace**

> "One of the things the president has initiated is really a look at procurement reform. And we’re big supporters of that because the more that we can streamline the processes... we’re going to take time out of the system, we’re going to take cost out of the system, without sacrificing safety or quality."
— **Larry Culp, CEO of GE Aerospace**

> "This is the ultimate long-cycle business; we’re going to continue to play the long game... to not only have another good 2026, but really put together a decade of outstanding performance that sets us up for the 2030s."
— **Larry Culp, CEO of GE Aerospace**

briefings.title: Anthropic and Alignment | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s refusal to allow the U.S. military to use its models for surveillance or autonomous weapons creates a fundamental conflict of sovereignty; if AI is as transformative as nuclear weapons, the U.S. government cannot tolerate a private corporation acting as an independent power base that dictates national security terms.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Anthropic’s refusal to allow the U.S. military to use its models for surveillance or autonomous weapons creates a fundamental conflict of sovereignty; if AI is as transformative as nuclear weapons, the U.S. government cannot tolerate a private corporation acting as an independent power base that dictates national security terms.

## The Anthropic vs. Department of Defense Standoff
* **Point of Conflict:** Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has restricted the U.S. military from using Claude for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, citing "democratic values" and current technical unreliability.
* **The Pentagon’s Response:** The Department of Defense (DoD) has threatened to designate Anthropic a “supply chain risk”—a label usually reserved for foreign adversaries—and may invoke the Defense Production Act to force the removal of these safeguards.
* **Competitive Landscape:** While Anthropic resists, OpenAI has recently reached an agreement with the DoD to allow its models to be used in classified settings, effectively replacing Anthropic in the military's tech stack.
* **The "Maduro Incident":** Tensions spiked after Anthropic officials expressed disapproval to Palantir regarding the use of their technology during a U.S.-monitored operation involving Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

## The Logic of Sovereign Power
* **The "International Law" Analogy:** Ben Thompson argues that international law is only as "real" as the entity capable of enforcing it; similarly, a private company cannot dictate terms to a state that possesses the ultimate monopoly on force.
* **The Nuclear Comparison:** Dario Amodei has compared selling AI chips to China to "selling nuclear weapons to North Korea."
    * **Consequence of the Analogy:** Thompson asserts that if AI is truly on the level of nuclear weapons, the U.S. government must treat it as a matter of existential national security that cannot be left in the hands of "unelected corporate executives."
* **A Binary Choice:** Thompson posits that the U.S. government faces two options regarding Anthropic:
    1. Force Anthropic into a subservient position where it yields decision-making power to the President and Congress.
    2. Remove the leadership or destroy the entity to prevent it from becoming a rival power base.

## Corporate Governance vs. Democratic Oversight
* **The Definition Problem:** Restrictions like "do not target civilians" sound simple but are "moral minefields." Thompson references Palmer Luckey (Anduril) to argue that definitions of "civilian," "innocent," and "autonomous" should be decided by elected officials, not CEOs.
* **The American Experiment:** There is a fundamental tension between a constitutional republic and a future where the "real levers of power" are outsourced to billionaires and their shadow advisors.
* **Enforcement Paradox:** Anthropic’s position that it can "align" the military is seen as untenable because the state cannot accept a dependency on a vendor that might withdraw support during an active conflict.

## Geopolitical Realism and AI Safety
* **The Taiwan Flashpoint:** The debate over AI is inextricably linked to the defense of Taiwan and TSMC. Thompson notes that Amodei’s push for strict chip controls risks "destroying AI for everybody" if China decides that if they cannot have AI, no one can.
* **The Fallacy of "Responsible Stewards":** Thompson critiques the idea that AI safety can only be managed by a few closed-source companies.
    * **Proliferation is Inevitable:** Massive incentives exist for others to build models, rendering "gatekeeping" ineffective.
    * **Open Source as Defense:** In a world of AI proliferation, the best defense against malicious AI is more AI, suggesting that open-source development may ultimately be safer than a closed-door oligopoly.

> "To the extent that AI is on the level of nuclear weapons — or beyond — is the extent that Amodei and Anthropic are building a power base that potentially rivals the U.S. military. Anthropic talks a lot about alignment; this insistence on controlling the U.S. military, however, is fundamentally misaligned with reality." — **Ben Thompson**

> "Do you believe in democracy? Should our military be regulated by our elected leaders, or corporate executives? Seemingly innocuous terms from the latter like 'You cannot target innocent civilians' are actually moral minefields... unelected corporations managing profits and PR will often have a very different answer." — **Palmer Luckey**

> "I believe deeply in the existential importance of using AI to defend the United States... [but] using these systems for mass domestic surveillance is incompatible with democratic values. AI-driven mass surveillance presents serious, novel risks to our fundamental liberties." — **Dario Amodei**

briefings.title: BREAKING NEWS: JD Vance Delivers Remarks To The International Association Of Firefighters In D.C.
briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance emphasized the Trump administration’s commitment to firefighters through proactive labor engagement, personal gratitude for their role in community stability, and specific legislative support for healthcare and retirement benefits.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance emphasized the Trump administration’s commitment to firefighters through proactive labor engagement, personal gratitude for their role in community stability, and specific legislative support for healthcare and retirement benefits.

## Support for Organized Labor and First Responders
* **Engagement with Unions:** Vance asserted that the administration has been "unique among Republicans" by actively seeking partnerships with organized labor, citing collaborations with Ed Kelly (IAFF) and Sean O'Brien (Teamsters).
* **The "Glue" of Communities:** He described firefighters, police, and military as a "brotherhood" that provides the essential security required for a functioning society.
* **Universal Public Safety:** Vance argued that the hallmark of the U.S. is that public safety services are not reserved for the wealthy but are accessible to everyone regardless of socioeconomic status.
    * **Equal Access:** "Every person deserves to know that if, God forbid, their house catches on fire, there's going to be somebody with water there to put it out, not just the powerful."

## Personal Connection to Fire and EMS Services
* **Impact of Opioid Crisis:** Vance shared a personal narrative regarding his mother’s struggle with addiction in Middletown, Ohio, noting that firefighters and EMTs provided critical support during her darkest moments.
* **A Success Story:** He credited first responders for his mother’s 11 years of sobriety, noting that her recovery allowed her to celebrate at the White House and become a grandmother to his children.
    * **Second Chances:** He highlighted that firefighters provide the "second chances" that allow families to stay together and recover from crises.

## Legislative and Policy Priorities
* **Social Security Fairness Act:** Vance credited President Trump’s leadership for ensuring congressional Republicans prioritized this legislation to benefit first responders.
* **Railway Safety Act:** Born out of the East Palestine train derailment, this act aims to address the long-term health consequences of toxic chemical exposure for first responders.
    * **Medical Research:** The administration appropriated millions to study the effects of toxic exposure to ensure firefighters receive proper long-term medical treatment.
* **Honoring Our Fallen Heroes Act:** Vance highlighted this law, which extends federal benefits to the families of firefighters who pass away from cancers developed in the line of duty.
    * **Earned Benefits:** He emphasized that these are not handouts but benefits "earned" through hazardous service to the public.

## Economic and Social Vision
* **Rewarding "Grit":** The administration's goal is to ensure the "American Dream" is attainable through hard work rather than luck or wealth.
* **Working-Class Focus:** Vance linked the specific needs of firefighters to broader national goals, such as:
    * Reversing inflation to ensure families do not live paycheck to paycheck.
    * Reducing crime rates to ensure first responders operate in safer environments.
    * Improving local schools to support the families of those in uniform.

> "We have been unique among Republicans in that we haven't turned away organized labor. We have tried to find ways to work with organized labor... to serve working people." — JD Vance

> "Every country, every empire, every society in history made it possible for a rich person to get what they needed. But what makes the United States so unique is that whether you're rich or poor... you have access to [public safety] in that critical moment." — JD Vance

> "When a firefighter... becomes ill or, God forbid, loses your life because of cancer that was developed in the line of duty, their families are entitled to federal benefits that they earned." — JD Vance

briefings.title: ETF Edge on crypto's rebound, the new ETFs to watch and what's different this time
briefings.tldr: Despite ongoing geopolitical turmoil in the Middle East, cryptocurrency is maintaining its role as a strategic portfolio diversifier with low correlation to traditional assets, while the industry shifts from a "crypto winter" toward institutional maturity through new index-based ETFs and regulatory-compliant infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Despite ongoing geopolitical turmoil in the Middle East, cryptocurrency is maintaining its role as a strategic portfolio diversifier with low correlation to traditional assets, while the industry shifts from a "crypto winter" toward institutional maturity through new index-based ETFs and regulatory-compliant infrastructure.

## Cryptocurrency as a Portfolio Diversifier
* **Low Asset Correlation:** **Simeon Hyman** notes that Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have shown "de minimis correlation" with equities and surprisingly low correlation with traditional safe havens like gold and silver.
    * During recent Middle East conflicts, Bitcoin has remained stable or risen slightly while equities have pulled back, reinforcing the diversification thesis.
* **The "Nuclear Winter" Bottom:** **Kim Arthur** suggests the market is currently in a "bottoming process" following a massive 50% drawdown in Bitcoin's price over the last year.
    * Recent price action (up 10% off the lows) is encouraging, signaling a potential thaw in the extended depressed period for the asset class.
* **Store of Value vs. Utility:** Speakers distinguished between Bitcoin as a "digital asset" or "store of value" and Ethereum/Solana as platforms with utility on the blockchain.

## ETF Innovation and Investment Strategies
* **Broad Indexing via CRYP:** ProShares recently launched the **ProShares CoinDesk 20 Index ETF (CRYP)** to provide an indexed approach to the top 20 cryptocurrencies.
    * **Quarterly Reconstitution:** Unlike typical equity indices that rebalance annually, CRYP rebalances quarterly to keep pace with the rapidly evolving crypto landscape.
    * **Capped Weighting:** The index caps Bitcoin and Ether at roughly 50% of the total weight (which would otherwise be 85% in a pure market-cap model) to capture the breadth of the ecosystem.
* **The Active Management Benchmark:** **Kim Arthur** argues that Bitcoin is the master benchmark for all crypto allocators.
    * If an active manager or an altcoin-heavy fund cannot outperform Bitcoin over a five-year horizon, the added turnover and risk of active management are rarely justified.

## The Stablecoin Infrastructure and the "Genius Act"
* **Reserve Asset Innovation:** ProShares launched the **ProShares Genius Money Market ETF (IQMM)**, the first ETF designed to comply with the "Genius Act" (clarity legislation for stablecoin reserves).
    * **Institutional Utility:** IQMM provides a 1940-Act regulated vehicle for the $250 billion stablecoin industry to use as a reserve, featuring same-day settlement and weekly distributions.
* **The Stablecoin Use Case Gap:** Current data shows that 80% of stablecoin activity is used for trading other cryptocurrencies. 
    * To achieve broad adoption, the industry must expand stablecoin use into traditional commerce and "buying stuff" outside the crypto ecosystem.

## Macro Outlook and Sector Rotation
* **Geopolitical Resilience:** Historical data from the Gulf Wars and the 12-day Iran war suggests that while markets initially pull back during Middle East conflicts, they typically rebound 25-30% in the following 6–12 months.
* **Shift to "Asset-Heavy" Plays:** **Main Management** has shifted its sector rotation strategy away from "asset-light" sectors (Technology, Communications) toward "asset-heavy" sectors:
    * **Basic Materials, Energy, and Industrials:** These sectors are benefiting from reshoring, manufacturing incentives, and the massive land and steel requirements for new AI data centers.
* **Market Sentiment:** **Kim Arthur** emphasizes that "fear is temporary, but greed is permanent," suggesting that regional economic interests (such as tourism and trade in Qatar and Dubai) will likely press for a swift resolution to current tensions.

> "Mitigating volatility in a portfolio means a lot because you can get 8% a year with low volatility; actually you'll compound to more than 10% with lots of volatility. So having diversified assets means a lot." — **Simeon Hyman**

> "Price and proof rarely happen at the same time. And Bitcoin was trading at 125,000 five months ago... I think we're doing the bottoming process in this nuclear winter." — **Kim Arthur**

> "I've been doing this for almost 40 years... there's been no less than nine times that the market has corrected 20 plus percent. But over that whole period, it's time in the market because the markets are up 10 plus percent." — **Kim Arthur**

briefings.title: The Future Of Brain-Computer Interfaces
briefings.tldr: Max Hodak, founder of Science and co-founder of Neuralink, discusses how the field of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) is shifting medicine from incremental drug discovery to a precise neural engineering paradigm capable of restoring sight today and potentially enabling human-to-human consciousness sharing by 2035.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Max Hodak, founder of Science and co-founder of Neuralink, discusses how the field of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) is shifting medicine from incremental drug discovery to a precise neural engineering paradigm capable of restoring sight today and potentially enabling human-to-human consciousness sharing by 2035.

## Restoring Sight: The PRIMA Retinal Implant
Science has successfully completed a clinical trial for its PRIMA implant, a breakthrough that restores "form vision" to patients with age-related macular degeneration.

*   **Technology Overview:** The system uses a 2x2mm silicon chip implanted under the retina.
    *   **Mechanism:** Patients wear glasses equipped with a camera and a laser projector. The laser hits the implant's "solar panels," which excite the bipolar cells directly.
    *   **Strategic Advantage:** By stimulating bipolar cells rather than the optic nerve, the device preserves the retina’s natural data compression/processing, resulting in coherent images rather than just flashes of light.
*   **Clinical Results:** Over 40 patients have received the treatment. One patient, blind for over a decade, was able to read a full novel after the procedure.
*   **Agnostic Treatment:** The technology is "disease-agnostic," meaning it can restore sight regardless of why the rods and cones died (e.g., Macular Degeneration, Stargardt’s, or Diabetic Retinopathy).

## The Neural Engineering Paradigm Shift
Hodak argues that the brain is effectively a computer with a well-defined "API," and engineering it is more efficient than traditional pharmaceutical approaches.

*   **Drug Discovery vs. Engineering:** Humanity is historically poor at drug discovery, which is often slow and incremental. Neural engineering allows for direct, empirical manipulation of the brain's information processing.
*   **The Brain’s API:** All information enters and leaves the brain through a limited number of "cables" (12 cranial nerves and 31 spinal nerves).
    *   **Latent Space:** Modern AI research has revealed that the "latent spaces" and representations in LLMs look remarkably similar to how the brain represents objects and faces.
*   **Neuroplasticity:** The brain is highly plastic under feedback. Even in adults, the cortex can learn to interpret new signals if given consistent feedback, allowing the brain and the BCI to "handshake" and learn together.

## The Next Frontier: Bio-hybrid Interfaces
Beyond electrical stimulation, Science is developing "bio-hybrid" interfaces that function like a biological "internet nerve."

*   **The "Avatar" Concept:** Inspired by the "ponytails" in the film *Avatar*, this involves growing engineered, stem-cell-derived neurons that wire directly into the host's brain.
*   **Immune Evasion:** Science has developed "hypoimmunogenic" stem cells that are hidden from the patient’s immune system, meaning the graft doesn't require a custom manufacturing process for every patient.
*   **Safety Profile:** Unlike gene therapy (a "one-way door"), the bio-hybrid approach only edits the graft cells. If the graft fails or dies, the patient's original brain tissue remains unmodified and unharmed.

## Vessel: Miniaturizing Life Support
Science's "Vessel" program aims to take "perfusion" technology—historically confined to hospital ICUs—and make it portable.

*   **The "Bridge to Nowhere" Problem:** Current heart-lung machines (ECMO) are massive and expensive, often creating ethical dilemmas when patients are kept alive but cannot leave the hospital.
*   **Miniaturization Goal:** Hodak envisions a world where a patient can carry a heart-lung circuit in a backpack or check a donor kidney as luggage on a commercial flight.
*   **Longevity Impact:** These advancements in perfusion and BCI lead Hodak to believe the first people to live to 1,000 years may already be alive today, as we move toward a future where the brain can be supported by "conscious machines."

> "I think it is very possible that the first people to live to a thousand are alive right now... Biotech has just been so incremental, but it no longer really feels so incremental to me. It feels like we're firmly in the takeoff era now." — **Max Hodak**

> "The brain is a computer and that's going to get me yelled at... but reality is whatever spikes are on the cranial and spinal nerves. In that sense, you've got this well-defined interface to it." — **Max Hodak**

> "If the end of the quest of artificial intelligence is super-intelligent machines, then I think the end of the BCI quest is actually conscious machines." — **Max Hodak**
